title: Emigration and Immigration
summary: Governs the heading Emigration and immigration and the free-floating subdivision --Emigration and immigration (and --Emigration and immigration--Government policy) under places, the class of persons heading Immigrants (divided by place of settlement, never by place of origin), Noncitizens, Migration, Internal, and Return migration. [place]--Foreign population and [place]--Emigration and immigration--Biography were cancelled in 1987; biography uses Immigrants--[place]--Biography. LC catalogers (2026) use LCGFT Biographies instead of --Biography.
validation_rules: Assign `Emigration and immigration` to general works on the process of resettling in a new country; it may be subdivided by `--History` or `--History--[century]`, e.g. `Emigration and immigration--History--20th century`. (H 1581 sec. D)

Use the free-floating subdivision `--Emigration and immigration` under names of regions, countries, cities, etc., for emigration from or immigration to a place, e.g. `California--Emigration and immigration`; `Mexico--Emigration and immigration`; it may be followed by `--History` or `--History--[century]`, e.g. `Italy--Emigration and immigration--History--20th century`. (H 1581 sec. E.1)
For migration from one country to another, assign `[place of origin]--Emigration and immigration` and `[place of destination]--Emigration and immigration`. (H 1581 sec. E.1)

Use `[place]--Emigration and immigration--Government policy` for government policies encouraging or discouraging migration, e.g. `United States--Emigration and immigration--Government policy`. (H 1581 sec. E.2)
`[place]--Foreign population` was cancelled in 1987; do not use it. (H 1581 sec. A)
`[place]--Emigration and immigration--Biography` was cancelled in 1987; do not use it. Use `Immigrants--Biography` or `Immigrants--[place]--Biography` instead. (H 1581 sec. A, F.3)

`Immigrants` is a class of persons heading covering both emigrants and immigrants; it takes the free-floating subdivisions for classes of persons (H 1100), e.g. `Immigrants--History--20th century`; `Immigrants--Government policy--United States`. (H 1581 sec. F.1, E.2 example)

Divide `Immigrants` geographically by the place in which they settled, e.g. `Immigrants--Ohio`; `Immigrants--Massachusetts--Boston--Biography`; this also covers works on immigrants and their descendants. (H 1581 sec. F.2)

Do not divide `Immigrants` by the place from which they came; bring out the country of origin with the ethnic group heading, e.g. `Portuguese--Massachusetts--History` + `Immigrants--Massachusetts--History`. (H 1581 sec. G.1)

For works on ethnic groups not discussing the immigrant generation, assign the ethnic group heading only, not `Immigrants` (e.g. `Italian Americans--Connecticut--Hartford--Economic conditions`). (H 1581 sec. G.2)

Assign `Noncitizens` to works on persons who are not citizens of their country of residence (e.g. `Noncitizens--India--History`); when they relocate without complying with legal requirements, also assign `Illegal immigration`. (H 1581 sec. H)

Assign `Migration, Internal` (e.g. `Migration, Internal--Prairie Provinces`) for movement within a country, and specific headings such as `Rural-urban migration`, `Urban-rural migration` for special aspects. (H 1581 sec. I)
Assign `Return migration` for works on social or demographic aspects of emigrants' return to their country of origin. (H 1581 sec. J)
When assigning `Emigration and immigration` or `[place]--Emigration and immigration`, generally also assign `Immigrants`. (H 1581 sec. K)

Related headings appearing in examples: `Children of immigrants--[place]`; `[ethnic group]--Foreign countries`; `[place]--Civilization--[ethnic] influences`; `[ethnic group] diaspora`. (H 1581 sec. F.2, K examples)
[LC practice] LC catalogers no longer use `--Biography`; assign `Immigrants` or `Immigrants--[place]` without it, and `655 #7 $a Biographies. $2 lcgft`. (H 1581 sec. A, F.3)

sections.heading: A. Background
sections.text:
Works on population movements are cataloged in various ways, depending on the nature of the material and the type of human movement discussed. The heading *Emigration and immigration* and the free-floating subdivision *--Emigration and immigration* are used for works on the process of leaving one's native land and moving to a foreign country in order to settle permanently. *Immigrants* is a class of persons heading used for works on foreign-born persons who enter a country intending to become permanent residents or citizens. *Noncitizens* is a class of persons heading used for works on persons who are not citizens of the country in which they reside. Headings of the type *[place]--Foreign population* and *[place]--Emigration and immigration--Biography* were cancelled in 1987. This instruction sheet provides guidelines for assigning the headings *Emigration and immigration*, *Immigrants*, *Noncitizens*, and related headings.

LC practice: As stated in H 1075, LC catalogers will no longer use form subdivisions. Instead assign an appropriate term or terms from Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms (LCGFT), e.g. *Biographies*. To replace a form subdivision that includes a demographic group, also assign Library of Congress Demographic Groups Terms (LCDGT) to bring out the audience of the resource being cataloged, e.g. *German speakers* or *Arabic, Students of*.

sections.heading: B. Recent revisions
sections.text: 2026-02: Updated template. Added instructions related to LCGFT implementation.

sections.heading: C. Definitions
sections.text:
Emigration: departure from a place of abode, natural home, or country for life or residence elsewhere.[^1]

Immigration: travel into a country for the purpose of permanent residence there.[^2]

[^1]: EMIGRATION Definition & Meaning - Merriam-Webster
[^2]: IMMIGRATION Definition & Meaning - Merriam-Webster

sections.heading: D. General works on emigration and immigration
sections.text:
Assign the heading *Emigration and immigration* to general works on the process of resettling in a new country, including the administration of the emigration/immigration process, the reasons why persons leave their native land, their arrangements for transportation and the moving of personal and household goods, their trip to another country, their arrival, etc. Subdivide the heading further by the free-floating subdivisions *--History* or *--History--[XX century]*, if appropriate.

Example:

```
Title: History of emigration in the 20th century.
650 #0 $a Emigration and immigration $x History $y 20th century.
650 #0 $a Immigrants $x History $y 20th century.
```

sections.heading: E. Specific regions, countries, cities, etc.
E.1. General
sections.text:
Use the free-floating subdivision *--Emigration and immigration* under names of regions, countries, cities, etc., for works on the process of emigration from or immigration to a place. Subdivide the heading further by the free-floating subdivisions *--History* or *--History--[xx century]*, if appropriate. For works on migration from one country to another, or to a particular place within another country, assign a heading to indicate the place from which emigrants came and a heading for the place to which they moved.

Example:

```
Title: Mexico to California : emigration and immigration.
651 #0 $a California $x Emigration and immigration.
651 #0 $a Mexico $x Emigration and immigration.
650 #0 $a Immigrants $z California.
650 #0 $a Mexicans $z California.
```

sections.heading: E.2. Government policy
sections.text:
Use the free-floating subdivision *--Emigration and immigration--Government policy* under names of regions, countries, cities, etc., for works on the policies adopted by individual governments to encourage or discourage specific types of migration, such as quotas for particular groups, lifting of restrictions for certain occupations, etc.

Example:

```
Title: The Caribbean exodus.
651 #0 $a Caribbean Area $x Emigration and immigration.
651 #0 $a United States $x Emigration and immigration.
651 #0 $a United States $x Emigration and immigration $x Government policy.
650 #0 $a Immigrants $x Government policy $z United States.
```

sections.heading: F.1. General
sections.text: Assign *Immigrants* as a class of persons heading to general works on persons who leave their native land and settle in another country in order to become permanent residents or citizens. Use this heading for emigrants as well as immigrants. Subdivide the heading further by the free-floating subdivisions used under classes of persons (H 1100), if appropriate.

sections.heading: F.2. By place
sections.text:
For works on immigrants in a particular place, divide the heading by the place in which they have settled. Assign a heading of this type also to works covering both immigrants and their descendants.

Example:

```
Title: Immigrants arriving in Ohio in 1985.
650 #0 $a Immigrants $z Ohio.
651 #0 $a Ohio $x Emigration and immigration.
```

```
Title: Australian immigration : the foreign-born population and their Australian-born children.
650 #0 $a Immigrants $z Australia $x History.
650 #0 $a Children of immigrants $z Australia $x History.
651 #0 $a Australia $x Emigration and immigration $x History.
```

sections.heading: F.3. Biography
sections.text:
Assign the heading *Immigrants--Biography* or *Immigrants--[place]--Biography* to works of individual or collective biography that are limited to, or include in a significant way, the experience of leaving one country and settling permanently in another.

LC practice: Assign a subject heading *Immigrants* or *Immigrants--[place]* to works of individual or collective biography that are limited to, or include in a significant way, the experience of leaving one country and settling permanently in another. Also assign LCGFT appropriate to the form and/or genre of the resource in hand, e.g. LCGFT *Biographies*.

Example:

```
Title: Patrick O'Casey : an immigrant in Boston.
600 10 $a O'Casey, Patrick, $d 1870-1920.
650 #0 $a Immigrants $z Massachusetts $z Boston $v Biography.
650 #0 $a Irish $z Massachusetts $z Boston $v Biography.
651 #0 $a Boston (Mass.) $v Biography.
LC practice:
600 10 $a O'Casey, Patrick, $d 1870-1920.
650 #0 $a Immigrants $z Massachusetts $z Boston.
650 #0 $a Irish $z Massachusetts $z Boston.
651 #0 $a Boston (Mass.)
655 #7 $a Biographies. $2 lcgft
```

sections.heading: G.1. General
sections.text:
For works on immigrants belonging to an individual ethnic group, assign a heading for the ethnic group and the heading *Immigrants*. Do not divide *Immigrants* by the place from which they came. Use instead a heading for the name of the ethnic group to bring out their country of origin.

Example:

```
Title: Portuguese immigrants in Massachusetts.
650 #0 $a Portuguese $z Massachusetts $x History.
650 #0 $a Immigrants $z Massachusetts $x History.
```

sections.heading: G.2. Descendants of immigrants
sections.text:
For works on individual ethnic groups that do not discuss the immigrant generation, assign a heading for the name of the group. Do not assign the heading *Immigrants*.

Example:

```
Title: The economic mobility of third and fourth generation Italian Americans in Hartford, Connecticut.
650 #0 $a Italian Americans $z Connecticut $z Hartford $x Economic conditions.
```

sections.heading: H. Noncitizens
sections.text:
Assign *Noncitizens* to works that discuss collectively persons who are not citizens of the country in which they reside, including recent immigrants, foreign students, foreign visitors, immigrants and nonciticzens who have entered illegally, military personnel, or government employees temporarily stationed in a foreign country, etc. When this heading is assigned to works on noncitizens who permanently or temporarily relocate across national borders without complying with the legal requirements of the destination country, the heading *Illegal immigration* is also assigned.

Example:

```
Title: A history of foreigners in India.
650 #0 $a Noncitizens $z India $x History.
```

sections.heading: I.1. General
sections.text:
Assign the heading *Migration, Internal* to works on the movement of persons from one place to another within the same country.

Example:

```
Title: Migration in the Prairie Provinces.
650 #0 $a Migration, Internal $z Prairie Provinces.
```

sections.heading: I.2. Special aspects
sections.text:
Assign headings for specific types of internal migration to works on special aspects of the topic, for example, *Rural-urban migration*, *Urban-rural migration*, etc.

Example:

```
Title: Urban migration and economic development in Nigeria.
650 #0 $a Rural-urban migration $z Nigeria.
651 #0 $a Nigeria $x Economic conditions $y 1960-
650 #0 $a Urbanization $z Nigeria.
```

sections.heading: J. Return migration
sections.text:
Assign the heading *Return migration* to works on the social or demographic aspects of emigrants' return to their country of origin.

Example:

```
Title: The brain drain : emigration to the United States and return.
650 #0 $a Brain drain $z Developing countries.
650 #0 $a Return migration $z Developing countries.
651 #0 $a Developing countries $x Emigration and immigration.
651 #0 $a United States $x Emigration and immigration.
650 #0 $a Immigrants $z United States.
```

sections.heading: K. Assigning additional headings
sections.text:
Works on emigration and immigration are usually multifaceted, requiring an array of headings to bring out various aspects of the material. Assign several headings, if appropriate, to cover the important topics discussed in a work, such as the individual ethnic group involved, the country from which they moved, the immigration process, the place in which they settled, the conditions in which they lived, the history of their descendants, etc. Generally, when assigning the heading *Emigration and immigration* or *[place]--Emigration and immigration*, assign also the heading *Immigrants*.

Examples:

```
Title: The life and hard times of the Rodriguez family in Chicago.
600 30 $a Rodriguez family.
650 #0 $a Immigrants $z Illinois $z Chicago $v Biography.
650 #0 $a Mexicans $z Illinois $z Chicago $v Biography.
650 #0 $a Mexican Americans $z Illinois $z Chicago $v Biography.
651 #0 $a Chicago (Ill.) $v Biography.
651 #0 $a Chicago (Ill.) $x Social conditions.
LC practice:
600 30 $a Rodriguez family.
650 #0 $a Immigrants $z Illinois $z Chicago.
650 #0 $a Mexicans $z Illinois $z Chicago.
650 #0 $a Mexican Americans $z Illinois $z Chicago.
651 #0 $a Chicago (Ill.) $x Social conditions.
655 #7 $a Biographies. $2 lcgft
```

```
Title: Japanese in Brazil.
650 #0 $a Japanese $z Brazil $x History.
651 #0 $a Japan $x Emigration and immigration $x History.
651 #0 $a Brazil $x Emigration and immigration $x History.
650 #0 $a Immigrants $z Brazil $x History.
651 #0 $a Brazil $x Civilization $x Japanese influences.
```

```
Title: Italian emigration in the 20th century.
651 #0 $a Italy $x Emigration and immigration $x History $y 20th century.
650 #0 $a Immigrants $x History $y 20th century.
650 #0 $a Italians $z Foreign countries $x History $y 20th century.
```

```
Title: Cultural assimilation of Chinese immigrant children.
650 #0 $a Chinese American children.
650 #0 $a Chinese Americans $x Cultural assimilation.
650 #0 $a Children of immigrants $z United States.
```

```
Title: Aportaciones e integración de los Vascos a la sociedad mexicana en los siglos XIX-XXI.
650 #0 $a Basque diaspora $x History.
650 #0 $a Basques $z Mexico $x History.
650 #0 $a Basques $z Mexico $x Social life and customs.
650 #0 $a Immigrants $z Mexico $x History.
650 #0 $a Basques $z Mexico $v Biography.
651 #0 $a Mexico $x Civilization $x Basque influences.
LC practice:
650 #0 $a Basque diaspora $x History.
650 #0 $a Basques $z Mexico $x History.
650 #0 $a Basques $z Mexico $x Social life and customs.
650 #0 $a Immigrants $z Mexico $x History.
650 #0 $a Basques $z Mexico.
651 #0 $a Mexico $x Civilization $x Basque influences.
655 #7 $a Biographies. $2 lcgft
```
